conclusion: Erdos #126 reduces in four elementary lines to a solution count for the unit equation: g(k) <= 2 + N(k+1) where N(r) bounds solutions of x+y=1 in a rank-r subgroup of Q*, so N(r)=exp(o(r)) implies the conjecture, and the known N(r) <= 2^{8r+8} is the same exponential wall the 1934 theorem sits at. The recommended program is not the reduction itself (its first step is a famous open problem strictly stronger than #126) but the m-base-point version, where each extra element of A adds a free simultaneous unit equation that no existing counting argument uses.
confidence: Lemma 2 and its corollary are proved here and machine-checked on a witness as exact rationals; lean on them fully, but note the reduction is almost certainly folklore inside the Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman method and is not claimed as new. The literature rows (g(k) <= 2^k from Erdos-Suranyi, GST 1986, Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman 1988, Beukers-Schlickewei 2^{8r+8}) come from search summaries and arXiv:2602.07545 because erdosproblems.com/126 returned HTTP 403; treat them as cited, not verified at source. The ranking of chains is judgment, not theorem.
